summary.text: CA9 has the strongest and most weight-robust convergent evidence. It ranks first in convergence (score 4.5197, 5 streams). It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269) and replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712, padj 2.58e-30). It keeps its fold change at purity 1 (log2FC 7.787). RCC cells carry 0.976 of its tissue transcripts, and it has a clinical-stage antibody (girentuximab, PHASE_3). It stays in the overall top 10 in 0.894 of random re-weightings. It is not prognostic (Cox log HR -0.009) and not a DepMap dependency (mean effect 0.051), so it is a targeting and imaging handle, not a functional vulnerability.

CD70 is the second surface antigen on which omics, literature and external knowledge agree. It is tumour-up at RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 7.09) and keeps a purity-1 log2FC of 4.278. The literature describes high, specific ccRCC expression as a HIF downstream target and reports CD70 radiotracers. Antibodies are in the clinic (cusatuzumab PHASE_2, vorsetuzumab mafodotin PHASE_1). As with CA9, the case rests on tumour-selective surface expression, not on dependency (DepMap mean effect 0.251).

NNMT is the strongest dual target-and-biomarker candidate. It is tumour-up (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein log2FC 2.709) and tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256). Higher expression predicts worse survival in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479), and the literature calls it a prognostic biomarker and potential target. It ranks 2nd in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.973). It has no clinical drug, so the target call is a small-molecule hypothesis.

Most of the rest of the convergence top 25 are proximal-tubule genes lost in tumour (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, PIGR) and the biomarker-profile leaders PSAT1 and ALDH6A1. Several are prognostic in TCGA, so they are best read as biomarkers of lost tubule identity, not as targets. The established drivers VHL and PBRM1 are mechanism. The clinically actionable node downstream of them is HIF-2alpha (EPAS1, belzutifan at APPROVAL), which ranks low on expression. None of the omics-convergent targets shows a selective DepMap dependency.

omics.text: CPTAC tumour-versus-normal omics split the candidates into two groups. Up-regulated, tumour-intrinsic genes (CA9, CD70, ENPP3, SCARB1, SLC16A3, NNMT, HK2) are up at RNA and protein, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and stay up when extrapolated to a pure tumour. They fit the hypoxic, glycolytic state that follows VHL loss. Down-regulated genes (PSAT1, ALDH6A1, SLC22A8, ALDOB) mark loss of normal tubule identity and carry prognostic information.

ALDH6A1 is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.399, protein log2FC -1.925). It sits in a frequently lost region (CNV loss frequency 0.355) with a positive copy-number-to-expression correlation (cis rho 0.525), and lower expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR -0.554). The dosage link gives it a plausible genomic cause for its loss, which few of the tubule biomarkers have.

FABP6 is the up-regulated candidate with the clearest copy-number support. It is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921), is gained in 0.573 of tumours with a positive dosage effect (cis rho 0.309), and replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 6.431). It has no ccRCC literature in the corpus, so its rank is data-driven.

literature.text: Literature and data converge most clearly for CA9, CD70 and NNMT (tumour-up targets), ENO2 (a tumour-up glycolytic gene with an adverse prognosis) and ALDOB and SLC22A8 (tumour-loss prognostic biomarkers). Only the CA9 PET and CD70 radiotracer work approaches translation, and both are early. Most other gene-level claims rest on one or two bioinformatic or cell-line studies. SCARB1, ENPP3, FABP6, HK2 and most biomarker-profile leaders have no extracted ccRCC relations in the roughly 320-abstract corpus, so their ranks are data-driven.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) has one mechanistic study: an in vivo CRISPR screen with anti-PD-1 found that SLC16A3-driven lactate export activates a GPR81-ERK-c-MYC loop, polarises macrophages toward M2 and suppresses CD8 T cells. This gives its strong omics profile an immune-evasion rationale, but the target case rests on a single paper and there is no clinical drug.

PSAT1 shows the clearest disagreement between data and interpretation. It is down in tumour, yet higher expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR 0.43). The only literature is a four-gene LASSO-Cox signature, which does not explain the direction. It is a usable prognostic marker but its biology is unresolved.

FCER1G is reported as abundant in tumours, linked to macrophage infiltration, T-cell suppression and an unfavourable prognosis, and prognostic under nivolumab but not everolimus. Its purity-1 log2FC drops to 1.061 from a bulk RNA log2FC of 2.499, so the signal is immune-derived. It is a microenvironment marker, not a tumour-cell target.

external.text: EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target. Belzutifan is at APPROVAL, and its Open Targets association score is 0.4871. Its DepMap signal is selective but modest (selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of ccRCC lines dependent, padj 0.061). It ranks only 38 in convergence because its RNA barely changes (log2FC 0.306) while the drug acts on the protein. This is the main disagreement between expression-driven convergence and clinical reality.

Open Targets, UniProt and DepMap split the tumour-up candidates by modality. CA9, CD70, ENPP3 and SCARB1 are membrane proteins. The first three already have antibody, ADC or radioligand programmes (girentuximab PHASE_3, cusatuzumab PHASE_2, AGS-16C3F PHASE_2). NNMT, SLC16A3, HK2 and SCARB1 have no clinical drug. None of them is a ccRCC dependency, so their tractability rests on surface accessibility, not on tumour dependency.

MTOR, the other established pathway target, has a strong ccRCC dependency (mean effect -1.52, 1.0 of lines dependent, padj 0.011) but is flagged as common essential, so selectivity (0.354) does not remove the toxicity risk. Expression convergence does not single it out (rank 56).

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-intrinsic at single-cell resolution. RCC cells carry 0.976 of tissue transcripts and, paired by donor, CA9 is higher in tumour cells than in proximal tubule (log2FC 7.739, padj 0.0189, 6 donors).

Several familiar ccRCC targets are not tumour-cell genes in this dataset. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of tumour transcripts), so anti-VEGFR drugs act on the vasculature. CD74 is held by macrophages and antigen-presenting cells, and CXCR4 by CD8 T cells (0.563 of transcripts). The bulk immune signal of FCGR3A drops at purity 1 (log2FC 2.191) and is infiltration-driven. CD70 and NNMT had no cell-type rows with evidence ids, so their tumour-intrinsic call rests on the bulk purity extrapolation.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.377, padj 0.00173), with a composition-corrected RCC share of 0.998. CA9 marks the tumour compartment in situ, which matches its single-cell and purity profile. Spatial context was not queried for the other candidates.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader (MGD) scores rank candidate sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, 1 accessible lysine). Ligand-site recall is 0.5 overall but only 0.221 in the top pockets, so it is a modest site. CA9 is already reachable by antibody, so a degrader is not the priority modality.

Among discovery candidates, RAB42 has the most confident model (mean pLDDT 85.31) and a best site scoring MGD 0.5348, but the pocket is small (37.4 A3) and unvalidated. CD70 has no structural analysis available.

discovery.text: In the tumour track, COL23A1 is the leading under-studied, undrugged candidate (novelty 0.839). RCC cells hold 0.881 of its tumour transcripts, it is up at RNA (log2FC 4.07) and protein (log2FC 2.51), vital-organ expression is low (3 nTPM, heart muscle) and it has no clinical drug. Its AlphaFold model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91, best site 8.0 A3), so an antibody is the realistic modality.

RAB42 is the second tumour-track candidate (novelty 0.775). RCC cells hold 0.627 of its transcripts, it is up at RNA (log2FC 3.11) and protein (log2FC 1.9), it has 2 ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, and vital-organ expression is low (2.6 nTPM, lung).

In the immune track, LRRC25 (macrophages hold 0.787 of tumour transcripts, 0 ccRCC papers, off-tumour bone-marrow expression) and GAL3ST4 (macrophages, antibody-tractable) stand out. In the stroma track, OLFML2A (fibroblasts) is weaker. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses with no dependency or functional evidence, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.

validation.text: External replication and the purity check strengthen the tumour-up targets. CA9, CD70, NNMT, SCARB1, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and HK2 all replicate in TCGA-KIRC and keep their fold change at purity 1, so their bulk signal is not infiltration. FCGR3A and FCER1G are weakened, because their bulk increase follows immune infiltration. Prognosis strengthens NNMT and the tubule-loss biomarkers (PSAT1, ALDH6A1, PCK1, SLC6A19, ALDOB, SLC22A8) but not CA9, CD70 or SCARB1.

Somatic driver status points to mechanism, not to the expression-ranked targets. VHL is mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483) and lost in 0.791 of tumours, but its expression change is modest (RNA log2FC -0.479). It acts through loss of function and HIF stabilisation, which drives the CA9 and ANGPTL4 programme.

Selective DepMap dependency weakens every omics-convergent target: CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SLC16A3, SCARB1 and HK2 show no ccRCC dependency. EPAS1 is the only candidate with a selective signal, and it is borderline. Protein-adjusted kinase activity does not inform the top candidates, because none of them is a kinase, and phosphosite analyses were not queried in this run.

robustness.text: Under 1000 random re-weightings, the target profile is stable at the top. SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3 and FABP6 stay robustly in the target top 10, and SCARB1 and CA9 have the narrowest intervals. In the biomarker profile only PSAT1, NNMT and ALDH6A1 are robust. ALDOB and SLC22A8 score high on average but have wide biomarker intervals. VHL's overall rank swings widely because it scores mainly on genetics. CA9 is the only gene robustly in the overall convergence top 10.

SCARB1 is the most weight-robust target-profile call (p_top10 0.968, 90% rank interval 1 to 8), even though it has no ccRCC literature in the corpus and no clinical drug. Its position rests on tumour-intrinsic up-regulation (purity-1 log2FC 3.762) and an Open Targets genetic association (0.519), not on knowledge-driven streams.

integration.text: Read together, the layers separate three groups. First, targets where omics, literature, external knowledge and cell context converge: CA9 and CD70, both tumour-intrinsic surface antigens with clinical antibodies. Second, data-strong targets with little prior knowledge: NNMT (also prognostic), SCARB1, SLC16A3, ENPP3 and HK2. Third, biomarkers of tubule-identity loss: PSAT1, ALDH6A1, ALDOB, SLC22A8 and PCK1. The disagreements are informative. EPAS1 is clinically validated but ranks low on expression, KDR is an endothelial target, and the lack of DepMap dependency for the convergent targets means they suit antigen-directed modalities better than inhibitors.

targets.rationale: Ranks 1 in convergence and 2 in the target profile (p_top10 0.941). It is tumour-up at RNA, protein and in TCGA-KIRC, carried by RCC cells (0.976 of transcripts), RCC-surrounded in situ, and targeted by girentuximab (PHASE_3). It is not prognostic and not a dependency, so it is best used as an antibody, radioligand or imaging target.

Tumour-up (protein log2FC 2.421), purity-1 log2FC 4.278, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.88), supported by ccRCC literature as a HIF-driven surface antigen, with cusatuzumab at PHASE_2. Placed above SCARB1 despite a lower target score because literature and clinical programmes converge on it.

Rank 2 in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.973) and robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.88). It is tumour-intrinsic (purity-1 log2FC 5.256), prognostic (Cox log HR 0.301) and supported by literature. With no clinical drug, the target call is a small-molecule hypothesis.

Top of the target profile (score 4.1314) and the most weight-robust target (p_top10 0.968). It is a tumour-up, tumour-intrinsic membrane protein with an Open Targets genetic association. Placed below CA9 and CD70 because it has no ccRCC literature in the corpus and no clinical drug.

Rank 1 in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.96). It is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -3.867), replicates in TCGA-KIRC and is prognostic (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7). It is an expression-loss biomarker, not a target, and the direction of its survival effect is unexplained.

Tumour-up membrane enzyme (RNA log2FC 3.895, purity-1 log2FC 5.278), robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823), with an ADC (AGS-16C3F) at PHASE_2. Corpus literature is absent and there is no dependency.

MCT4 lactate transporter, tumour-up (protein log2FC 2.279), purity-1 log2FC 3.821, robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.881), with a single-study immune-evasion mechanism. It has predicted tractability but no clinical drug or dependency. It ranks only 15 overall because the overall score mixes in biomarker streams.
Robust biomarker (p_top10 0.808). It is down in tumour, with copy-number-linked loss (cis rho 0.525) and the strongest prognostic effect in the list (Cox log HR -0.554).

Rank 2 overall. It is strongly down (RNA log2FC -7.028), and lower expression predicts worse survival (Cox log HR -0.358), which literature supports. Placed lower because its biomarker-profile interval is wide (90% interval 2 to 99) and its signal reflects lost proximal-tubule identity.

Rank 4 overall. It is strongly down (RNA log2FC -6.715) and prognostic (Cox log HR -0.402), with single-study literature support. Its biomarker-profile interval is very wide (1 to 194), so its position depends on the weights.

Included despite a low convergence rank (38) because it is the approved ccRCC target (belzutifan) and the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal (selectivity 0.3, padj 0.061). Its weak RNA change shows that expression convergence misses targets that act at the protein level.

limitations.text: All omics are bulk tumour-versus-normal comparisons. The ranking is associative, not causal, and protein fold changes are compressed by TMT ratios.
No omics-convergent target shows a selective DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines, so the targets are supported for antigen-directed modalities, not as functional vulnerabilities.

The literature corpus is small (about 320 ccRCC abstracts), and most gene-level claims rest on one or two, often bioinformatic, studies. The literature agent did not read the full convergence ranking.

Single-cell context comes from one cohort with small proximal-tubule groups. Cell-type rows with evidence ids were not available for CD70 or NNMT, and EPAS1, MET and EGFR were not examined by the cell agent.
MGD scores rank structural sites and are not evidence that a degrader exists. Ligand-site validation was available only for CA9.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency or functional evidence, and their literature counts are by gene symbol.
Phosphosite and kinase-activity analyses and STRING interactions were not queried, and PNCK, TNFAIP6, FABP6, CYP2J2 and ANGPTL4 were not profiled for druggability.
